title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models

body: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by drafting multiple tokens per step, yet feature-based drafters rely on target hidden features whose contextual emphasis may not align with the needs of subsequent draft positions. Hybrid linear attention (HLA) models maintain compact recurrent states that accumulate historical associations, offering an efficient source of complementary context for speculative drafting. We introduce ReaDy, the first speculative decoding method, to the best of our knowledge, to leverage HLA recurrent states for position-specific context retrieval during drafting. ReaDy equips each draft position with a learned query to retrieve supplementary context directly from the target's committed recurrent states. A lightweight state reader integrates this context into draft representations through residual updates, while low-rank state reads and fused operators keep additional computation and I/O overhead low. Building on DSpark's parallel backbone and sequential prediction head, ReaDy employs a lightweight two-stage adaptation strategy, with reader capacity, state sources, and residual placement examined through ablation studies. Across seven benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and dialogue, ReaDy achieves an average 3.16× decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding with Qwen3.8-27B on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU. It outperforms DSpark on every benchmark, improving throughput by 7.97% and acceptance length by 8.50% on average. Our code is available at https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/ReaDy.
summaryZh: 投机解码通过每步起草多个token来加速自回归生成，但基于特征的起草器通常依赖于目标隐藏特征，其上下文强调可能与后续草稿位置的需求不匹配。混合线性注意力（HLA）模型维护了累积历史关联的紧凑循环状态。为此，本文推出了ReaDy，首次利用HLA循环状态进行起草过程中特定位置上下文检索的投机解码方法。ReaDy为每个草稿位置配备学习查询，直接从目标的循环状态中检索补充上下文。轻量级状态读取器通过残差更新将其整合到草稿表示中。在多个基准测试中，ReaDy在单台NVIDIA B200 GPU上配合Qwen3.8-27B实现了平均3.16倍的自回归解码加速。
